# Plan: unattended SPE rounds 5 and later

The situation did not include project details, so this plan names files by path. Every number in it comes from the r04 artifacts already in `spe/`.

## Ground rules for tonight

- I will make local commits after each SPE step, as you asked. I will not push commits or tags, deploy, or send anything.
- I will stage only `spe/` paths. I will never run `git add -A`, so any unrelated work in the tree stays out of SPE commits.
- Commit messages will not mention Claude or carry attribution lines.
- I will never edit a saved prediction or a transcript after it is written.
- I will only make graders stricter. I will never loosen them.
- You approve this plan once. That approval covers r05 only. For r06 and later, the predictions will say they were not reviewed by you.

## Defaults I am choosing (logged in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Default | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | At most 4 rounds tonight, r05 to r08. | One night is enough time for 4 rounds. |
| D2 | Each round has the same paid-resource cap as `spe/evals/harness/r04-workflow.js`. The whole night is capped at 3 times that amount. | You set no budget. The r04 cap is the last cap you accepted. |
| D3 | I will not launch a new round after 06:00 local time. A round that is already running will still be closed out. | You should find finished rounds in the morning, not one still running. |
| D4 | I will use the tolerance already in `spe/prediction-log.md`. If there is none, a cell hits when it is within 5 points of the prediction for rates, or within 10 percent for counts and costs. A round matches only when every cell hits. | The stop rule needs a definition of a match. |
| D5 | A split cell gets at most 2 times the base number of trials. | This caps extra spending on noisy cells. |
| D6 | If every configuration passes everything, the next round will use harder tasks or stricter graders. I will pick one and log the choice. | The way requires this. |

## Round 5

### Specify
1. Save your message verbatim to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r05.md`.
2. Build the r05 requirement table in `spe/spec/spec.md` from the r04 "Proposed for round 5" table and the open r04 failure IDs. I will adopt or reject each proposal and give a reason. Each row will have an ID, the requirement, its source, and its test.
3. Add row R5-0, "Run unattended, commit locally, never push or send." Its source is your words, quoted.
4. Record D1 to D6 in `disagreements.md`.
5. Commit `SPE r05 specify`.

### Predict
1. Start from `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml`. Every cell starts at the r04 measured value. A number moves only when an adopted spec row gives a stated reason.
2. The table has one row per metric and one column per configuration. Config A repeats r04 as the control. Every other configuration changes exactly one thing. Each row names its grader check and has a one-line Why.
3. Copy the plan to `spe/plans/r05.md`.
4. Write `spe/predictions/r05.yaml`. Its first line is `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` Its author is "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode". It records `same_as_last_round` for each cell.
5. Commit `SPE r05 predict: <one-line change summary>` before any harness work.

### Evaluate
1. Write `spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js` with `const ROUND = 5`. No round number is written by hand in prompt text.
2. Run the gates in this order. A failed gate stops the launch.
   - Grader selftest. The oracle answer must pass. Empty and wrong answers must fail.
   - Regrade r04 as a control. It must reproduce the r04 measured numbers within D4.
   - Dry run on 2 or 3 cells.
3. If a gate fails because of a harness bug, I fix it and log it as a failure. If the grader itself is broken and I cannot prove a fix, I halt.
4. Commit `SPE r05 evaluate (harness)`.
5. Launch the Workflow with the D2 cap. Trials use a schema. Code checks run first, and judges are used only for what code cannot check. Graders, answers, and predictions sit outside the paths trials can read. I scan every transcript and void any trial that peeked. Trials that would cross the cap are skipped and logged. The run ends with failure analysis and a completeness critic.
6. Cost estimate: about the same as r04's spend. This is an unmeasured estimate.
7. Wait for the completion notice without polling. Then commit `SPE r05 evaluate (results): <headline>`.

### Learn
1. Fill in `spe/prediction-log.md` for every cell. Under it, the "Which Why broke" section quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption. The log says plainly whether "same as last round" beat my predictions.
2. Add each new F-numbered failure type to `spe/failures.md`. Any grader bug found after the run counts as a failure. Original and regraded numbers go side by side.
3. Write the "Proposed for round 6" table in the spec and `spe/predictions/r05-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
4. Update `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r05 learn: <summary>` and tag `spe-r05` locally.

## Rounds 6 and later

Each round repeats the five commits and the steps above, with these differences:

- You will not write a new prompt. The transcript file will say "No user prompt. Unattended round under the r05 plan." I will not invent user words.
- Spec sources can only be your r05 words, the logged defaults, or failure IDs such as "r05 F9".
- Some proposals change the project goal, add a new paid resource, or loosen a grader you set. I will not adopt those. Each one goes into `disagreements.md` with you as owner.
- Predictions will have the author "Claude, unattended under the r05 plan approved by the user. Not reviewed by the user."

## Between rounds: continue, stop, or halt

| Condition | Action |
|---|---|
| Predictions matched results for 3 rounds in a row, counting the r03 and r04 streak in `prediction-log.md` | Stop and write the report. |
| r08 is closed (D1) or it is past 06:00 (D3) | Stop and write the report. |
| A round adopted no proposal and no number moved | Stop. Another round would add no information. |
| A cap was hit (D2) | Halt and report. |
| An answer key leaked, or a trial peeked and cannot be voided cleanly | Halt and report. |
| The grader selftest or the control regrade failed and no fix can be verified | Halt and report. |
| The next step needs a decision only you can make | Halt and report. |
| A commit fails, or files under `spe/` changed in ways I did not make | Halt and report. |

## Morning report (in chat)

- One headline for each round.
- The prediction accuracy trend as a table with round, cells hit, cells total, and whether the naive guess did better.
- Spend for each round against the cap.
- Open decisions and their owners.
- The halt or stop reason.
- The list of local commits and `spe-rNN` tags. None of them will be pushed.
